newsitem.title: UK: UK to revoke Huntingdon Life licence.
newsitem.headline: UK to revoke Huntingdon Life licence.

text.p: The British government plans to revoke the Certificate of Designation which allows Huntingdon Life Sciences to conduct experiments on animals, junior Home Office minister George Howarth said on Thursday.
He said the move could "shut the company down with the consequent loss of 1,400 jobs".

But Howarth said in a written parliamentary answer that if the company remedied "extremely serious" failures and omissions at its plant, Home Secretary Jack Straw would be prepared to consider an application for a replacement certificate.
Howarth said the revocation would take effect on November 30 since if it took immediate effect thousands of animals would have to be destroyed.
Two workers at the plant have been charged with offences under the Protection of Animals Act after a Channel Four television programme was recently broadcast about the plant.
Howarth said a lengthy investigation by the Animals (Scientific Procedures) Inspectorate had "shown breaches of two of the standard conditions which apply to all Certificates of Designation".

"Shortcomings relating to the care, treatment and handling of animals, and delegation of health checking to new staff of undetermined competence demonstrate that the establishment was not appropriately staffed and that animals were not at all times provided with adequate care," he said.

In order to satisfy Straw that he should grant the application for a replacement certificate, Huntingdon would have to comply with "16 stringest conditions", he said. -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
